{"id": "75:16/q13", "question": "How is this instruction connected to other Qurʾānic passages?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "75:16/q13/p1", "position": "It parallels 20:114, which forbids hastening the Qurʾān before revelation is complete.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī also cites 87:6. {"id": "75:16/q14", "question": "How does the instruction fit the sūra's surrounding argument?", "turns_on": "Whether the command is an occasion-driven aside, a thematic transition, or part of the judgment scene.", "positions": [{"id": "75:16/q14/p1", "position": "It is a timely aside during revelation, after which the resurrection discourse resumes.", "reasons": "Al-Khaṭṭābī and al-Rāzī compare a teacher or speaker briefly correcting a distracted listener. Al-Suyūṭī says the opening reached 75:15 as the Prophet hastened, and 75:16–19 intervened. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls it etiquette interrupting the resurrection account. Al-Rāzī says six contextual explanations answer an allegation of textual loss. Al-Ṭībī says Gabriel inserted the instruction at 75:15 and the recitation resumed at 75:20, like a teacher correcting a rushed pupil; al-Ālūsī calls this interruption account far-fetched and unsupported."}, {"id": "75:16/q14/p2", "position": "It is linked thematically by haste, conscience, speech, and the need for divine guidance.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī ties unbelievers' pursuit of immediate happiness to religious haste, fear of forgetting, knowledge of their own falsity, and reliance on God; Abū Ḥayyān contrasts denial of signs with the Prophet's eager preservation. Al-Bayḍāwī says even haste in religion is reproved. Elmalılı integrates conscience and revelation; al-Suyūṭī moves from the human soul to the Prophet's soul. Al-Sāmarrāʾī links the reproaching soul, spoken excuses, 75:20, omitted elements, and gathering bones and Qurʾān; he also notes plural and singular divine forms. Al-Biqāʿī ties self-reproach to the accusation of human speech at 74:25–26. Iṣlāḥī relates the instruction to pressure from opponents. Abū Ḥayyān contrasts a denier absorbed in desire with a believer preserving, studying, and presenting God’s signs in hope of acceptance; al-Ālūsī objects that the denier’s discussion is still in progress when this instruction appears."}, {"id": "75:16/q14/p3", "position": "The verses continue the resurrection record scene rather than introducing a prophetic aside.", "reasons": "Al-Balkhī and al-Qaffāl invoke the surrounding self-witness and record passage; al-Jishumī finds this contextual fit stronger while conceding the prophetic reading is more apparent. Al-Suyūṭī and al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reject it on the revelation report and 20:114. Al-Balkhī and his followers prefer continuity with 75:13: an implied saying introduces a circumstantial clause when the book is presented. Al-Qaffāl sees the ensuing detailed account and punishment as a severe threat."}, {"id": "75:16/q14/p4", "position": "The seeming break prompted an allegation of missing or altered text.", "reasons": "Al-Khaṭṭābī records the objection that 75:16–19 separates 75:14–15 from 75:20–21. Al-Rāzī attributes alteration allegations to early Rāfiḍīs; al-Suyūṭī records a Shiʿite allegation of dropped material. Abū Ḥayyān repeats al-Rāzī's report. Al-Khaṭṭābī, al-Rāzī, and Abū Ḥayyān answer with contextual connections."}, {"id": "75:16/q14/p5", "position": "The command interrupts the threat to heighten the terror of the Day and warn against demanding its date.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports that the Day is the pronoun’s referent and that God will assemble creation, describe the Day in the Qurʾān, and reveal it at the blast; he finds this account seriously difficult."}]}
{"id": "75:16/q15", "question": "How are the following verbs about loving immediate life and leaving the Hereafter read?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "75:16/q15/p1", "position": "The following verbs yuḥibbūna and yadharūna are read in the third person or second person.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī reports the third-person reading from Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb, and the second-person reading from the others."}]}
{"id": "75:16/q16", "question": "How is the command syntactically attached in the record reading?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "75:16/q16/p1", "position": "It is a circumstantial sentence at the presentation of the record, introduced by an implied saying.", "reasons": "Al-Balkhī and his followers derive the record from 75:13 and favor this construction."}]}
{"id": "75:17/q01", "question": "Why does the promise begin with inna?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q01/p1", "position": "It links the command against haste to God's guarantee and emphasizes that extraordinary guarantee.", "reasons": "Al-Sāmarrāʾī says the particle supplies a causal connection that would be lost without it, comparing 9:103; perfect retention and reproduction after hearing alone also call for emphasis."}]}
{"id": "75:17/q02", "question": "What does 'upon Us' say about God's undertaking?", "turns_on": "Whether divine obligation rests on the promise or on the wisdom required for prophethood.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q02/p1", "position": "God undertakes and guarantees the gathering and recitation of revelation.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr calls ʿalaynā a guarantee in both clauses; al-Rāzī and Jishumī observe that ʿalā conveys obligation. {"id": "75:17/q03", "question": "Why is 'upon Us' placed before 'its gathering'?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q03/p1", "position": "Fronting 'upon Us' restricts the guarantee to God alone.", "reasons": "Al-Sāmarrāʾī says God alone can gather, preserve, and enable accurate complete recitation; later placement would remove exclusivity and change the sense. {"id": "75:17/q05", "question": "What is meant by God's gathering it?", "turns_on": "Whether gathering concerns revelation retained in the Prophet, its assembled portions, or eschatological evidence and people.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q05/p1", "position": "God fixes the revelation in the Prophet's breast or heart for secure memory.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk describe placing it in his chest or establishing it in his heart. {"id": "75:17/q06", "question": "Why pair 'its gathering' with 'its qurʾān'?", "turns_on": "Whether qurʾān adds the act of reciting, specifies a kind of gathering, or itself means gathering.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q06/p1", "position": "The second term specifies or adds to the general act of gathering.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī says general gathering can be paired with the specific Qur'an or recitation, unlike 'reading people'; the second term can add a sense as 'warn' adds to 'inform.' {"id": "75:17/q07", "question": "What does 'its qurʾān' mean, and whose recitation is promised?", "turns_on": "Whether qurʾān denotes recitation or collection, and on the recitation sense whether the immediate reciter is Muhammad, Gabriel, or God.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q07/p1", "position": "God enables the Prophet himself to recite the revelation reliably.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk call qurʾān a verbal noun of reading; the Prophet recites after it is fixed in his heart. Jishumī includes repeating and explaining it; al-Bursawī specifies ordered joining of letters and words."}, {"id": "75:17/q07/p2", "position": "Qurʾān means collection, composition, or arrangement of revelation.", "reasons": "Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Qutayba derive the name from joining sūras. The she-camel or woman carrying no fetus, ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's لم تقرأ جنينا, water collected in a basin and its maqrāh, and a gathered qarya attest qaraʾa as collecting; al-Zajjāj relates the name to collected speech. Jishumī and al-Ṭabrisī compare the verbal-noun forms rujḥān and nuqṣān. Al-Ṭabarī says both composition and clarification are valid Arabic, while each revealed verse bound the Prophet before full compilation. Al-Ālūsī questions the reported composition account, though he also records its etymology."}, {"id": "75:17/q07/p3", "position": "God recites the revelation to the Prophet so that he understands or retains it.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī and al-Wāḥidī explicitly add understanding; Muqātil and al-Rāzī connect recitation with memorization and freedom from forgetting, the latter comparing 87:6. Al-Wāḥidī contrasts Gabriel as reciter with the Prophet on al-Zajjāj's interpretation."}, {"id": "75:17/q07/p5", "position": "Qurʾān is the verbal noun 'recitation,' without identifying a single reciter here.", "reasons": "Al-Farrāʾ equates qirāʾa and qurʾān as verbal nouns; al-Samīn and al-Ālūsī cite Ḥassān's nightlong recitation verse, as does Ibn ʿĀshūr. Al-Bursawī compares ghufrān; Ibn ʿĀshūr adds furqān; Elmalılı also allows the recited text as the noun's sense, and al-Nasafī compares 20:114."}, {"id": "75:17/q07/p6", "position": "It means collecting the recitation in the Prophet's chest.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī reports this alternate sense and calls the noun a verbal form like rajḥān and nuqṣān; Ibn ʿAṭiyya also reports collection and arrangement in the breast."}, {"id": "75:17/q07/p7", "position": "It is God's reading of the person's deeds or record at resurrection.", "reasons": "The record interpretation makes the reader acknowledge its contents and face explanation through requital; al-Qaffāl calls it a strong warning but notes lack of reports. Al-Qaffāl says God reads the assembled deeds to their owner, who must acknowledge or consider them; the ensuing explanation is of their consequences and punishment."}, {"id": "75:17/q07/p8", "position": "It is God's revelation of Judgment's description.", "reasons": "A reported interpretation says the gathering is of Judgment's people and its explanation comes with the trumpet blast. The alternative reported by al-Ālūsī specifies revelation of the Day's conditions in the Qur'an before its manifestation at the blast."}]}

{"id": "75:17/q11", "question": "What happened as the Prophet received revelation, and why did he hurry?", "turns_on": "Whether haste chiefly reflected fear of forgetting during recitation, or also concern for understanding and receiving guidance for the mission.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q11/p1", "position": "He moved his tongue or lips during Gabriel's recitation, fearing loss or forgetting, then listened and recited after Gabriel left.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās describes the strain of revelation, and Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd demonstrate the movement. Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it by multiple routes; Bukhārī also has him lower his head as Gabriel arrived. Al-Tirmidhī is cited by Elmalılı. Qatāda's version also ascribes the movement to fear of forgetting. Al-Ṭabarī distinguishes hurried reception before gathering from later memory review, which he finds chronologically less fitting. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the fear account as obscuring the command to follow the completed recitation; he also calls the report's fit with the verses obscure. The Imam suggests the Prophet's haste may have been expressly permitted before the prohibition; al-Ālūsī finds that explanation problematic."}, {"id": "75:17/q11/p2", "position": "He eagerly sought further revelation for his mission and guidance amid pressure from opponents, as well as fearing loss.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī says his opponents demanded answers and challenged piecemeal revelation; pauses had divine wisdom, yet the Prophet looked heavenward for help. Revelation renewed strength, guided his strategy and spiritual, moral, and intellectual needs, and enabled responses. Farāhī adds fear of responsibility for even one lost letter. Al-Zamakhsharī says he also hurried to ask about meaning; al-Rāzī contrasts reliance on repetition with turning to God, comparing 20:114. Al-Ālūsī favors al-Zamakhsharī's account over the Judgment-day alternative as better fitting the Qur'an's eloquence and subtle indications."}]}
{"id": "75:17/q12", "question": "What should the assurance teach about receiving and studying revelation?", "turns_on": "Whether the instruction is applied specifically to the Prophet's reception or also to every later reader and listener.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q12/p1", "position": "The Prophet should listen patiently, trust God's preservation and timing, and attend to the revealed portion and its meaning.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī says fear of forgetting is answered by divine aid; al-Jishumī stresses reflection and knowledge of meanings and rulings over mere memorization. Iṣlāḥī links patience to gradual revelation and 20:114–15, the Prophet's noble motives, and his duty to convey and explain; al-Zamakhsharī says questions about meaning wait until recitation ends."}, {"id": "75:17/q12/p2", "position": "Every Qur'an student should read attentively and grasp the whole message before hasty conclusions.", "reasons": "Asad extends the passage to anyone reading, listening, or studying, compares 20:114, warns against isolated verses, mechanical fluency, and attraction to sound without meaning, and sees one integrated message rather than detached maxims, narratives, or laws. Study Quran likewise calls for reflection on all teachings."}, {"id": "75:17/q12/p3", "position": "Do not hurry to ask when the Day will come; God will disclose its conditions and manifest it in due course.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports this alternative as a prohibition on opening one's mouth to demand the Day's date; its timing rests on divine wisdom, while the Qur'an reveals its conditions and the blast manifests it."}]}
{"id": "75:17/q13", "question": "What does the promise imply about preservation of the received Qur'an?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q13/p1", "position": "The Qur'an has been guarded against loss, addition, and textual alteration.", "reasons": "Al-Naḥḥās rejects a claim that some remained unrevealed; Sufyān contrasts God's direct care of the Qur'an (15:9) with Torah and Gospel entrusted to their people (5:44). Al-Zarkashī invokes 15:9 and communal agreement that the codex is certain and protected for practice. Farāhī cites 41:41–42 and 15:9 and reports communal agreement. Named Imāmī authorities reject disappearance; al-Qummī calls the codex precisely the revelation without an extra letter, and Murtaḍā says weak dissenting reports cannot defeat certainty."}]}
{"id": "75:17/q14", "question": "When and how were the Qur'an's parts collected and ordered?", "turns_on": "The distinction between memorized and ordered revelation in the Prophet's lifetime and Abū Bakr's later gathering from existing materials.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q14/p1", "position": "The entire revelation was memorized and arranged during the Prophet's life, with divinely guided placement and final recitation.", "reasons": "Al-Zarkashī says the four famous Companion preservers were examples, not the only memorizers, while noting an exception concerning Barāʾa. Iṣlāḥī says the Prophet instructed collectors where verses belonged and reviewed extant revelation with Gabriel each Ramadan, twice in the final Ramadan. Farāhī infers an ordered sequence from the instruction to follow the recital, says it matched the Guarded Tablet, cites whole sūrahs recited and memorized in order, and says agreed authentic reports make Gabriel's final recitation settle doubts."}, {"id": "75:17/q14/p2", "position": "After Yamāma's heavy losses, Abū Bakr commissioned Zayd to gather written and memorized Qur'an.", "reasons": "Al-Bukhārī's Zayd report says ʿUmar feared further deaths among reciters, persuaded a hesitant Abū Bakr despite the Prophet not having performed this collection, and Zayd, a trusted young revelation scribe, assembled material from writing media and memories after his own hesitation."}]}
{"id": "75:17/q15", "question": "How does this verse fit its surrounding passage?", "turns_on": "Whether 75:16–19 form an instructional interruption or continue and echo the surrounding resurrection theme.", "positions": [{"id": "75:17/q15/p1", "position": "Verses 75:16–19 interrupt the resurrection account to instruct the Prophet about revelation.", "reasons": "Al-Khaṭṭābī reports the objection that they disrupt movement from self-witness (75:14–15) to love of worldly life (75:20–21). Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī accepts an interruption and compares 20:114, adding that an interruption needs no overt signs before and after it; al-Bayḍāwī sees a rebuke of haste even in revelation."}, {"id": "75:17/q15/p2", "position": "The revelation passage is integrated with the sūra's account of conscience, impatience, and gathering.", "reasons": "Elmalılı joins the preceding conscience discussion to the end of the passage; al-Sāmarrāʾī compares God's gathering of bones and of sun with moon at Judgment to earthly gathering and reciting of Qur'an. Al-Rāzī compares the unbeliever fleeing God with the Prophet's need to turn from repetition to God. {"id": "75:18/q04", "question": "What do the pronouns referring to 'it' designate?", "turns_on": "Who is addressed in 75:16–19 and whether those lines are an inserted instruction about revelation or continue the resurrection scene.", "positions": [{"id": "75:18/q04/p1", "position": "The Qurʾān being revealed to the Prophet.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr identifies the object with the Qurʾān in 'do not move with it'; Elmalılı says the implied antecedent is sufficient as at 97:1, since the addressee is the Prophet and Qurʾān is subsequently named. {"id": "75:18/q12", "question": "What does the verse teach about receiving and using revelation?", "turns_on": "Whether the direct instruction to Muhammad also guides every later reader and listener.", "positions": [{"id": "75:18/q12/p1", "position": "Wait patiently for revelation, attend to it, trust God's preservation, then recite and practice it.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj forbids premature recitation; Ibn Kathīr describes collection in the heart, enabled recitation and divine explanation as three stages. Al-Bayḍāwī says haste is blameworthy even in religion's foundation. Al-Biqāʿī extends following to fluent repetition and character-forming practice. Iṣlāḥī adds that God determines timing, collection, arrangement and elucidation; the Prophet can accept each portion without anxiety or heeding demands for revelation at once.
